scope: Source-level consistency audit of the 16 fd records in audit-sample.json
reviewer: LLM agent; not an independent human auditor

provenance.address_mapping: Every sampled FUN address is the corresponding ELF symbol address plus the analysis image base 0x100000. The mapping was checked against the non-stripped binary symbol table; stripping does not change these virtual addresses.

hashbrown 0.16.1.qualification: The binary contains /rust/deps/hashbrown-0.16.1 paths, so the observed copies can be compiler-vendored rather than the Cargo package despite the matching locked version.

object 0.37.3.qualification: object is absent from fd Cargo.lock. The version comes from /rust/deps/object-0.37.3 embedded in the binary and is part of the compiler/sysroot dependency set.

checksum_note: The extracted registry trees contain .cargo-ok and .cargo_vcs_info.json but no .cargo-checksum.json. Where Cargo.lock applies, the cached .crate SHA-256 was compared with the lock checksum and matched.

clear_label_problems: fd-09 combines two different closure expressions in fd::walk::WorkerState::build_overrides
neutral_boundary_cases: fd-11 is one shared machine address carrying two distinct walkdir Error method symbols and must remain neutral

records.member_evidence: All five addresses map, after subtracting 0x100000, to separate ELF-local symbols for this same method. The sole source definition is inside unsafe impl Automaton for NFA at lines 176-322.
records.reasoning: The concrete receiver type and method body resolve to one source definition. The five emitted copies are compatible with code-generation duplication or use-site instantiation; source review cannot recover their compiler origin IDs.

records.reasoning: There is one Debug derive site for Memchr2. The fmt body is macro-generated and has no explicit source span, so this is source-consistent with macro-expansion uncertainty rather than independent proof of generated-item identity.

records.reasoning: The function is generic over E, and all six emitted bodies point to the same explicit source definition. The concrete E types are not recoverable from the demangled names used here.

records.member_evidence: All six rebased addresses resolve to HashMap::insert in ignore, globset, regex_automata, or lscolors codegen units. The binary contains /rust/deps/hashbrown-0.16.1 source paths; the six symbol hashes are distinct.
records.reasoning: The source and binary version evidence support one generic 0.16.1 method instantiated for several types. Cargo.lock also contains hashbrown 0.15.5, but no sampled member was tied to that version; exact compiler-vendored revision identity remains unproved.

source.excerpt: builder.add(pattern).map_err(|e| anyhow!("Malformed exclude pattern: {}", e))?; ... builder.build().map_err(|_| anyhow!("Mismatch in exclude patterns"))

member_findings.FUN_0027a400: ELF 0x17a400 is a 104-byte closure that performs formatting before constructing anyhow::Error; this matches the line-339 |e| closure with a formatted error value.
member_findings.FUN_0027a470: ELF 0x17a470 is a 71-byte closure that loads a fixed 28-byte message before constructing anyhow::Error; this matches the line-344 |_| closure with the literal Mismatch in exclude patterns.

records.reasoning: The two members are not monomorphizations of one closure. They correspond to two syntactically and behaviorally different closure expressions whose normalized symbols collapse to the same parent-function closure name.

records.reasoning: This is source-consistent as a purposeful shared-address record and supports the neutral policy. It does not establish one source-definition family; treating the two symbols as a positive same-definition pair would be wrong.

records.reasoning: The source body and compiler-vendored version are consistent with the singleton record. The crates.io source is a reference copy, not proof of the exact sysroot source revision.

records.member_evidence: All 52 rebased addresses form a contiguous set of ELF-local symbols for this Display::fmt item, each with its own symbol hash and specialization-specific constants or formatting references.
records.reasoning: The generic B/P implementation is a single explicit source definition; the many bound-marker specializations explain the large group. Exact B-to-address assignments and compiler origin IDs were not established.

limitations: This review establishes source-level consistency, not rustc DefId or mono-item identity.
Trait implementations, derive output, closures, reify shims, and generic monomorphizations can share normalized names while representing distinct compiler items.
